notes: Registered portal: the global portal 'humana-tricare' (form_url …/home/index?ProviderType=PT — this exact PT form) is what template e842e237 'Humana Tricare' v3 action 1 fills; its library holds the extension's one-page capture of the same 60 controls (all on page_step 'Page 2'). See humana-tricare.template-diff.md.

The form is opened as …/home/index?ProviderType=PT; formUrl stays query-free per the contract. Without the parameter the page says 'Provider Type invalid.' Fetched with ProviderType=OT the markup is identical except #Selectedspecialty's options (OT taxonomy codes) and the script's provtype — so other ProviderType values keep the same rows but change the specialty vocabulary and the provider-type-keyed rules (step 1's required questions and the hidden #IsStudent question for other types; MFT adds a home address; BA/ABA/BT add board certification; facility types use the BH*/Fac*/ACSP sections that sit hidden in the same DOM). Capture each provider type as its own portal key.

One URL, four steps. The page keeps all four steps laid out and collapses the closed ones to height:0 / overflow:hidden, so nothing is positively hidden: probe v2 saw all 60 controls on every step and gave every step the same fingerprint. Probe v3 (this branch) leaves clipped-away controls out of a page (counted in offPage). The extension's own scanner and fill still see every step at once — a fill from step 1 would write all four steps — and DYN-PAGE-01 never splits these pageSteps (the URL's last segment is 'index', which matches no step name).
pageStep = the open step's legend; the page h1 ('Provider certification application') is the same on every step.

Continue / Back / Submit are <a> links (a.certApp--form__NB / __PB, Submit = #certApp--form__submit), not buttons — probe v3 reads links as navigation when their caption reads as an action. The anchors have no ids, so the advance selectors are nth-child chains under the step's fieldset id (#\31 … #\34 ).

Validation messages are <label class="required"> elements the page inserts after the question. The probe's error selector doesn't read them (that class is also how many forms mark required captions), so every gate here was read from those labels by hand. Also: the primary-specialty message is inserted after #specialityerror, next to #providertype — it belongs to #Selectedspecialty.

Validation is staged: a blank Continue shows only some messages (step 2 listed specialty, telehealth and point-of-contact name/email first, then NPI, Medicare # and ZIP once those were filled). Per the page script step 2 also validates first/middle/last name, gender, email, DOB, SSN, the point-of-contact address/city/state/phone, and a server-side active-duty check; step 3 validates every address part, both ZIPs, the age range (min ≤ max), hours and the license block. Only the messages actually seen are recorded as gates.

Step 1: for a PT all four questions are required and any 'Yes' is refused ('Not authorized to proceed with certification.' / 'Unable to continue with application as … not independently certified.'). #IsStudent (hidden for PT) is asked of other provider types.

#Selectedspecialty (primary specialty) is a select2 widget: the native <select> is aria-hidden="true" and 1×0 with the visible .select2-container beside it. The scanner skips it (zero box), so it was added by hand (origin user_mapped). The extension's fill would also skip it today — isHiddenControl treats aria-hidden as hidden (DYN-PAGE-02) — so it needs select2 support in the scanner and the fill before it can be filled. Its option values are NUCC taxonomy codes.
#MedicareNumber is optional but format-checked when filled ('Medicare number is invalid.'); it is not recorded as a gate because blank passes.

Step 3's Continue POSTs the location to /Home/AddLocation (and 'Add another practice location', #addLocation, POSTs it and clears the block for the next one — never clicked). Several locations = the step 3 block repeated, one AddLocation per location.

Address verification: after the fields pass, Continue opens a popup (#AddressReveal) whose buttons come from a server-rendered /Home/ValidateAddress partial — use the suggested address (SaveAddress) or keep the entered one (CancelAddress) — and Continue must be clicked again. The user resolved it during the walk; the partial's markup was gone by the time it was inspected, so the dismissSelector is inferred from the page script's CancelAddress handler and is unverified.

Hours: each day's Open/Closed select (default Closed) reveals that day's start/end pickers when set to Open, prefilled 08:00/18:00. Claude set Monday–Friday to Open with the user's OK to capture them (revealedBy). Step 3's fingerprint is the arrival set (all days Closed, 0a966732); with Mon–Fri open the same page hashes 13c56f45, so a runner should match the arrival keys as a subset.
Not walked on step 3: 'Any disciplinary action' = Yes reveals #LicComments (textarea) and enables the license upload; #AvailableHome/#AvailableOffice radios stay hidden for PT.
required mirrors HTML attributes, which this portal sets on optional inputs too (#mi, the apt/suite fields, #MedicareNumber, #PracticeFax); the gates are the real requirements.

Label fixes are in displayLabel only (label keeps the probe's text): the probe borrowed the SSN caption for #gender, the city captions for #CorrespondenceState and #PractBillingState, the license-number caption for #RestrictedLic, and the section legend for every Yes/No radio group.
Options over the panel's 50-option cap: #providertype (77), #CorrespondenceState and #PractBillingState (51), #MinAge and #MaxAge (99). They fail a send until mintedpanel#518 deploys.

Walk: Claude clicked No on the four step-1 questions and set Mon–Fri to Open (both with the user's OK) and clicked Continue only through `advance` controls; the user typed every step 2–3 value. Step 4 was left blank. Nothing was submitted.
